privacy_page_description: Read how the Mistria Field Guide stores your Fields of Mistria progress, handles feedback, and protects your privacy.
privacy_short_body: The Mistria Field Guide stores your data on your device only. Nothing is collected automatically or shared without your action. If you choose to send feedback, see below for what that includes.
privacy_device_heading: What is stored on your device
privacy_device_body: To remember your progress, the Mistria Field Guide saves your game data (completed items, settings, and world state) in your browser's local storage. This data never leaves your device unless you explicitly choose to send it.
privacy_feedback_intro: The Mistria Field Guide includes an optional feedback feature. When you submit feedback, the following is sent to the server:
privacy_feedback_item_versions: The app version and game data version (for debugging context).
privacy_feedback_item_selection: If you pick a specific item, its name, category, and page (no personal information).
privacy_feedback_item_progress: Your tracked progress data (items checked off, skill levels, etc.), only if you opt in.
privacy_feedback_item_email: Your email address, if you choose to provide one.
privacy_feedback_public_before_bold: Your feedback (minus your email) is used to create a
privacy_feedback_public_middle: on the GitHub issue tracker so I can find and fix problems. This includes your message, the item you picked (if any), and your progress data (if you opted in). Avoid including personal information in your message, as these fields will be
privacy_feedback_email_storage: If you provide an email address, it is stored privately in a separate system and never appears in the public issue. It is used only to follow up on your feedback if needed.
privacy_abuse_body: The feedback endpoint may use Cloudflare's built-in rate limiting or other abuse-prevention measures, which process IP addresses transiently at the network edge. IP addresses are not read, logged, or stored by the application.
privacy_third_party_body: The Mistria Field Guide does not use any analytics, advertising, or tracking services. The feedback feature uses GitHub (for public issue tracking) and Cloudflare (for hosting and rate limiting).
privacy_ai_body: The Mistria Field Guide is built with the help of AI coding tools that assist with writing & reviewing code. These tools operate on the project's source code & on user-submitted feedback (your message text & game progress, if you opt in). An AI service will never have access to your email address or any information about how you use the app.
privacy_changes_body: If this policy ever changes, I will update this page.
privacy_sync_intro: Syncing your save file is opt-in, so none of this happens unless you set it up. If you do, here’s what changes. Everything under “Without sync” still applies to the rest of your data.
privacy_sync_what_body: Only the game’s save file gets synced. Anything you check off by hand stays on that device. Your save file is end-to-end encrypted before it leaves your gaming computer, so only devices with your code can read it. We can’t read it, and neither can the server that passes it along.
privacy_sync_storage_body: The server keeps only the latest save file for each code, and deletes it 30 days after it was sent. It also keeps a small record for each code, with no save data in it: when the code was made and last used, how many save files were sent that day, a number that keeps save files in order, and one-way fingerprints that prove your computer owns the code and spot a repeat of the same save file. That record isn’t encrypted. It goes away when you make a new code, or a year after your last save file, leaving only a marker so the code never gets reused. One catch: Cloudflare, who hosts that server, keeps a recovery copy of its storage for 30 days, so a replaced or deleted save file can stay recoverable for up to 30 more days, still encrypted.
privacy_sync_code_body: Anyone holding your code can read the save files you share, until you make a new one. Treat it like a password, and it’s worth keeping off stream. If it ever gets out, make a new code and the old one stops working.
privacy_sync_ip_body: Cloudflare processes IP addresses to deliver your save file and to limit how often one address can ask for it, and we don’t log them. We also limit how many new codes can come from one address, without saving the address in our storage. All we keep is a count in an hourly bucket shared with lots of other addresses, so it can’t point back to you. Those counts can stay in Cloudflare’s recovery copy for 30 days too.
privacy_sync_account_body: There’s no account, no sign-in, and no email address. Your code is the only thing connecting your devices.
privacy_sync_turnstile_body: When you make a new code, Cloudflare Turnstile checks that you’re not a bot, with nothing for you to solve. That check is covered by Cloudflare’s {addendum}.

sync_only_save_phone: Only the game’s save file gets synced; anything you check off by hand on this phone stays here. Easiest is to do all your tracking right here, and let your gaming computer just read the save file.
sync_fresh_title: FYI, this is a fresh start
sync_fresh_body: You’ll be starting fresh by syncing your save file, which means anything you’ve tracked on this device will be cleared. Your save file will check off nearly everything on its own, but you can make a quick backup first if you’d like.
sync_find_intro: Gonna be honest, this is the weirdest part of the setup. But once you’re done here, it’s smooth sailing!
sync_find_other_os: On Linux, Steam Deck, or a Mac?
sync_find_linux_hint: Not there? Look in your Steam library’s steamapps/compatdata/2142790 folder.
sync_find_open: Now open File Explorer and paste that into the address bar at the top. It should take you to a folder with files like {file}. Drag that autosave file into this box:
sync_find_open_linux: Now open your file manager, press Ctrl+L, paste that, and press Enter. It should take you to a folder with files like {file}. Drag that autosave file into this box:
sync_find_open_mac: Now open Finder, press Shift-Command-G, paste that, and press Return. It should take you to a folder with files like {file}. Drag that autosave file into this box:
sync_find_drop_locked: Copy the folder first, and this box will wake up.
sync_find_bad_file: Hmm, we couldn’t read that one. Pick the newest file that ends in “autosave”.
sync_find_cant_drag_body: Copy the save file to your Desktop, then choose it from there. We can’t watch a copy, though, so you’ll need to do that again after you play.
sync_find_help_bar: Make sure you pasted it into the address bar at the very top of File Explorer, not the search box.
sync_find_help_run: Still nothing? Press the Windows key + R, paste the same folder location, and press Enter. (That only opens a folder. Never paste anything else into that box, from us or anyone.)
sync_farm_title: Perfect! Looks like that save file is for {farmer} on {farm}, is that right?
sync_farm_title_unnamed: Perfect! We found a farm in that save file. Is it yours?
sync_farm_no_hint: No worries! Pick the newest file that ends in “autosave”.
sync_phone_title: Wanna track this on your phone?
sync_phone_body: Or another device. Scan this code with it, and it’ll sync your save file from here on out.
sync_phone_copy_link_sub: For a computer with no camera
sync_phone_stream: Live on stream? Maybe don’t show this bit.
sync_phone_later: Okay, I’ll set it up later

sync_done_watched: While this tab’s open, we’ll sync your save file every time you sleep. So leave it open while you play!
sync_done_redrop: Whenever you’re done playing, drop your save file in again and we’ll sync it.
sync_share_skipped: Skipped. Show a code any time from Data.
sync_scan_title: Scan the code from your gaming computer
sync_scan_body: On your gaming computer, open {url} in Chrome or Edge and go through the steps there. When it shows a code, scan it here.
sync_scan_bad: Hmm, that link doesn’t look quite right. Try scanning the code instead?
sync_got_it_body: Your farm as of {time}. We’ll keep up from here.
sync_got_it_note: Anything you check off by hand on this device stays here.
sync_waiting: Your code works, but there’s no save file waiting yet. Open the tracker on your gaming computer, and we’ll grab the latest one.
sync_waiting_note: Nothing on this device changes until a save file arrives.
sync_ios_title: Quick question: here, or the home screen app?
sync_ios_body: Safari can clear a site’s data if you don’t visit for a week. The home screen app hangs on to it.
sync_ios_app_steps: Tap Share, then “Add to Home Screen”. Open the tracker from your home screen, tap “Sync from my farm automagically”, and scan the code there.
sync_switch_body: This device will start getting a different save file. If it’s a different farm, we’ll back up the current one, but only one backup fits, so you might want to make your own first.
sync_already_here: Your save file is already on this computer.
sync_retired_title: Your computer stopped sharing this save file
sync_retired_body: If it made a new code, scan it here. Or stop syncing and keep tracking by hand.
sync_unreadable_away_title: Your computer is having trouble reading your save file
sync_unreadable_away_body: Your progress is safe! For more info, check Mistria Field Guide on your computer.
sync_unreachable_body: We’ll keep trying, or you can try again.
sync_paused_setup: We’ve paused save file syncing for a bit to keep things running smoothly. It’ll turn back on by itself, usually by tomorrow. You can make your code later from Data.
sync_too_many: Whoa, that’s a lot of new codes! Give it a few minutes and try again.
sync_blocked: Before we can sync your save file, this device’s data needs a look. Head to Data to sort it out.
